attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own essay, stated in his own voice.

semantics.note: Firm 'will' with no hedge, so it is a forecast. The proposition keeps the 'entering an era' framing, and the financial-limit clause stays attached to trimming customer experience.

contract.note: The plain reading (several companies test automation and service cuts against a financial limit) is ordinary and fair. It rightly treats the money-losing clause as material, and with no deadline, absence of losses cannot contradict the claim.

evidence.note: Klarna's own 2024 release on AI handling customer chats while keeping live agents. Shows automation, but no financial stopping point.
Report on Wendy's AI ordering pilot and expansion. The CEO cites labour efficiency, with no loss threshold or harm.
Klarna spokesperson calls new human hiring a small pilot. This is a company statement and shows no financial boundary caused by automation.
Klarna's 2025 20-F describes AI running alongside human support. This is a company disclosure and does not settle the industry-wide forecast.

reviews.rationale: The packet shows companies running automation pilots (Klarna, Wendy's). No item links service cuts to a tested or discovered financial stopping point, and the claim has no deadline. The evidence does not settle the outcome either way.

attribution.note: Zitron's own statement in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Isn't currently' is a present-state observation. The parenthetical forecast is correctly split into a separate claim.

contract.note: In the strike context, 'replacement' as usable professional screenwriting without substantial human rewriting is an ordinary, fair reading. Using July 2023 as the reporting window is reasonable.

evidence.note: 2022 Dramatron co-writing study. It predates the target period and tests assistance, not replacement.
July 2023 report on a watchable AI South Park demo. It was short, unreleased and human-curated, so it does not show replacement of professional writers.

reviews.rationale: The packet has no representative July 2023 evaluation of whether AI could do professional screenwriting work. The demo falls short of replacement, and the 2022 study is from an earlier period. The evidence does not settle the observation.

attribution.note: Zitron's own parenthetical belief, stated in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'Nor do I believe it will be' is a firm expectation, not graded confidence. The 'for some time' horizon is preserved.

contract.note: Fair not to impose a fixed number of years on 'for some time'. The replacement standard is an ordinary reading. Without a deadline, the result depends on whether an early event clearly conflicts with the claim.

evidence.note: AI-credited feature filmed in January 2024, with the director cutting scenes. It is an experimental candidate, not independently judged to meet the professional standard.
June 2026 report of a producer using Claude for outlines but keeping a screenwriter. Shows one workflow, not general capability.

reviews.rationale: 'For some time' sets no deadline. The single AI-scripted film is an experiment that was not independently judged a professional replacement, so it does not clearly conflict with the forecast. Continued use of human writers does not settle it either.

attribution.note: Zitron's own prediction, stated in his own essay.

semantics.note: 'I believe we are going to see' is a firm expectation. The proposition keeps the surge, the disregard for consequences, and 'several smaller' Knight Capital-like failures.

contract.note: Reading 'several' as at least three and requiring material losses that fit the Knight analogy is ordinary and fair. With no deadline, absence of incidents cannot contradict the claim.

evidence.note: Secondary summary of 2024 corporate AI investment growth. Context for a 'surge', but it does not link spending to any failure.
Replit's own account of the database deletion. The data was fully restored and no financial loss is shown, so it does not qualify.
Amazon disputes that AI caused a limited outage. The incident is contested, with no material loss documented.

reviews.rationale: Investment growth is shown, but no item documents three post-publication AI failures with material losses tied to reckless deployment. The inspected incidents involved no loss or are disputed. The claim has no deadline, so it remains unresolved.
